summary_html:
No matching published aggressive prostate cancer baseline is available. These saved summaries use the HR ≈ RR ≈ OR identity approximation; provide incidence in Settings for baseline-dependent calculations.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 1.04 (95% CI: 0.34–3.21), indicating no statistically significant association between betaine and aggressive prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 88.09%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
